Summary (auto): Quick discovery on embedding and reranking architecture. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a mid-size analytics product with ~200k documents to start, target p99 latency < 200ms for top-k retrieval + rerank, throughput 100-300 QPS bursts. Discussed vector DB integration (Qdrant/Pinecone), dimensionality tradeoffs (1536 vs 768), hybrid search with BM25, batching/ingestion, and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pricing and benchmark sheet; customer to provide sample dataset.

Topics: embeddings model choice, vector DB, dimensionality, hybrid search, throughput, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, security/compliance

Action Items (recorded): see metadata section.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex here, AE, and with me is Priya from SE.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. We should have about 45 minutes to an hour, happy to go deep on the infra stuff you care about.
[00:22] Samir (Cobalt): Hey, Samir — ML Eng. We're evaluating embedding/re-ranking for our docs search. Want to understand where Redwood fits.
[00:30] Jo (Cobalt): Jo here — product. Focus is relevance + latency, also cost.
[00:36] Liam (Cobalt): Liam, CTO — I'll listen for security and infra implications.
[00:42] Alex: Great. High level — you mentioned 200k docs to start, can you confirm?
[00:48] Samir: Yeah roughly 200k now, long term maybe 2–3M. Query load currently 50–100 QPS with spikes to ~300 for peak reports. P99 latency target for retrieval+rerank is under 200ms ideally.
[01:05] Priya: Got it. Are you currently using a vector DB? Which one?
[01:10] Samir: We're prototyping with Pinecone for embeddings, and also had experiments with Qdrant. For text indexing we use Elastic for BM25. Thinking hybrid search — semantics + BM25 for recall.
[01:21] Alex: Sounds typical. The tradeoffs we'll discuss are: hosted API latency/cost, Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private for strict data residency.
[01:30] Samir: Important callouts — we need audit logs and KMS integration, SOC2 compliance. Also SAML SSO for our org.
[01:40] Liam: And we may want the control plane in our VPC if we go Private.
[01:45] Priya: Redwood Private supports VPC and customer-managed networking; we can talk about KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. I'll drop the security pack after.
[01:53] Jo: For embedding dims we're torn — 1536 vs 768. What do you typically recommend?
[02:00] Priya: Depends on your base model and downstream reranker. 1536 (e.g., OpenAI/Redwood-embed-like) gives better semantic fidelity but higher storage and CPU at search time. 768 often is a sweet spot for speed and cost. Also hybrid search with BM25 reduces need for massive dimensionality sometimes.
[02:18] Samir: Our reranker is a cross-encoder (bert-ish) that adds 50–150ms per top-k candidate, so we need a small candidate set from the vector DB.
[02:28] Alex: Right — typical pattern: use vector DB for top 100, then cross-encoder rerank top 10–20. That keeps end-to-end latency reasonable.
[02:36] [02:36] Priya: Question — what vector DB are you planning to run? If Pinecone vs Qdrant vs Milvus there are integration differences.
[02:45] Samir: We're leaning Qdrant for on-premish control, Pinecone for hosted simplicity. We also consider Elastic hybrid search.
[02:53] Priya: Redwood works with all — hosted Redwood API can return embeddings and do rerank server-side, but if you want to keep index in Qdrant/Pinecone you can push embeddings to them. For Dedicated we can colocate with your vector DB or run Redwood-managed indexes — depends on the architecture.
[03:12] Jo: For throughput, can Redwood Dedicated handle 300 QPS with sub-200ms p99?
[03:18] Priya: Yes, with the right config. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. For embedding generation we scale horizontally; for search we optimize kernel selection, batching, and KV cache management. We often recommend caching top queries and prefix caching for conversational flows.
[03:33] Samir: How about ingestion — large bulk upload of 200k docs, doing embeddings? Any tooling?
[03:38] Alex: We'll share a sample ingestion script and benchmark spreadsheet (link in notes). You can batch embeddings, choose dimensionality, and parallelize pushes to the vector DB. For Hosted, we have rate limits; Dedicated lets you run at higher sustained throughput.
[03:53] [03:53] Jo: Pricing wise — cost per token vs cost per embedding — concerned about unit economics.
[04:00] Alex: We'll send a Dedicated trial SKU and a cost estimate. Also the Optimize toolkit can suggest batching/quantization to lower cost.
[04:09] Samir: For reranking, is there a Redwood-managed reranker or do we host our own cross-encoder?
[04:14] Priya: We support both. Redwood can host a lightweight reranker or you can host on your side and call Redwood only for embeddings/generation. For private deployments customers often bring their own reranker in the same VPC for latency.
[04:29] Liam: Encryption at rest and KMS — any constraints?
[04:33] Priya: For Private and Dedicated we support customer KMS integration; hosted can use Redwood-managed KMS but we do support bring-your-own keys for enterprise customers.
[04:45] Samir: Any limitations on vector dimensionality or index types? We may want HNSW for recall and IVF for large scale.
[04:52] Priya: Most vector DBs support those. For memory/latency tradeoffs, we can advise on index params. Also quantization is an option if you want smaller footprint with small quality drop.
[05:05] [05:05] Jo: Hybrid search — how is that architected with Redwood?
[05:10] Priya: Two patterns: 1) Hybrid client-side: run BM25 in Elastic for recall, then combine candidates with vector DB, dedupe, and rerank. 2) Vector DB native hybrid (some support BM25-like fields). We usually recommend client-side hybrid for more control, though managed solutions exist.
[05:28] Samir: We need reproducible benchmarks. Can you share a spreadsheet with expected throughput numbers and recommended cluster sizes for Dedicated?
[05:36] Alex: Yes — Priya will attach a benchmark sheet showing QPS vs latency for sample configs and model dims.
[05:43] Priya: Quick note: some product names in benchmarks are shorthand; we sometimes call the product "Redwood Dediated" in transcriptions, sorry — but it's Dedicated. Also KV cache may show up as K V cash in some transcriptions.
[05:55] [05:55] Liam: Security checklist — SOC2, SAML, audit logs, data residency — any blockers?
[06:01] Priya: We have SOC2, support SAML/SSO, audit logs, and for Private deployments we can keep the control plane in your VPC. I'll send the security pack and SOC2 report link.
[06:12] Jo: For the initial POC scope — what would you recommend we try first?
[06:16] Alex: Typical POC: ingest 200k docs, run embedding generation with 1536 and 768 dims, load into Qdrant or Pinecone, run hybrid retrieval + rerank for a sample query set, measure p50/p95/p99 and relevance. We'll help with scripts and run a Redwood-hosted benchmark then repeat on Dedicated/Private as you prefer.
[06:36] Samir: Sounds good. For host vs dedicated — what are the SLA and price deltas?
[06:42] Alex: Hosted is pay-as-you-go with usage-based pricing; Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing with lower per-unit costs at commit and SLA-backed availability. I'll include numbers in the pricing doc.
[06:53] [06:53] Priya: One more technical — when you do reranking, how many candidates do you fetch? If your cross-encoder is slow, fetching top 100 then reranking to 10 is common. We can also do hybrid pre-filtering.
[07:06] Samir: We'll likely start with 100 -> rerank top 10.
[07:10] Jo: Any reference customers similar to us?
[07:13] Alex: We can share a few case studies; I'll include them in follow-ups.
[07:18] [07:18] Priya: Performance considerations for vector dims: at 1536 dims and 2–3M vectors, you should plan for larger memory footprint and maybe use quantization or IVF shards. For 768 dims memory and compute drop roughly by half.
[07:34] Samir: When you say quantization, what's the typical quality hit?
[07:38] Priya: Usually small — maybe 1–3% drop in recall depending on quant method and model. We'll surface that in the benchmark sheet.
[07:48] [07:48] Liam: If we want full control, Private is attractive but more ops on our side, right?
[07:53] Priya: Correct. Private gives you control (VPC, KMS), but you operate the infra. We can do a managed Private where Redwood handles ops under an enterprise contract.
[08:05] Samir: For end-to-end latency, any tips to shave p99 down?
[08:09] Priya: Use smaller candidate sets, optimize index params, use GPUs for rerank if needed, enable prefix/KV caching, and colocate services to reduce network hop.
[08:20] Jo: Do you have an SDK for hybrid orchestration or is it custom?
[08:24] Alex: We have SDKs and examples for hybrid flows; I'll link a repo and the deck.
[08:30] [08:30] Priya: I'll also include an ingestion script that parallelizes embedding generation and pushes to Qdrant/Pinecone.
[08:36] Samir: For our security team, what's the turnaround to get SOC2 docs and KMS integration details?
[08:42] Alex: We can supply SOC2 reports within 24 hours and a KMS integration guide; expect 2–3 business days for full security pack.
[08:52] [08:52] Jo: If we wanted to run the reranker in our VPC, is there an easy way to integrate Redwood embeddings?
[08:57] Priya: Yes — Redwood provides APIs to stream embeddings or batch export, and for Dedicated/Private we can mount a private endpoint in your VPC.
[09:06] Samir: Any pitfalls with Pinecone vs Qdrant?
[09:09] Priya: Pinecone is managed and simpler; Qdrant gives you more control and on-prem options. Qdrant's useful if you need to tune HNSW params directly. We'll include recommended index configs.
[09:22] [09:22] Alex: Ok let's capture next steps and responsibilities.
[09:25] Jo: Quick clarification — can Redwood do rerank server-side and return final ranking to the client?
[09:30] Priya: Yes, Redwood can host rerankers and return final results, or you can host reranker in your infra. Both supported.
[09:37] Samir: For the benchmark, please include p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k queries for the different dims and index configs.
[09:46] Alex: Will do.
[09:49] [09:49] Priya: I'll attach the benchmark sheet and ingestion example to follow-up.
[09:54] Liam: And I'll have our security lead review the SOC2 and KMS docs once sent.
[09:59] Jo: If we get good numbers on Dedicated, we'll consider a 6-month commit.
[10:05] Alex: Great — we'll propose a Dedicated trial and pricing.
[10:09] [10:09] Samir: Anything else?
[10:11] Alex: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the tech deep-dive.
